$comment: c52 (D-FFI-MATH-INFINITY): ship INFINITY from <math.h> as a FLOAT constant. sqlite uses `(double)INFINITY` at runtime (sqlite3.c:37393/37423) -> S0001 INFINITY undeclared. The integer `constants` surface is integer-only (a float there fails loud F_ShippedLibUnsupportedType); a float-valued macro ships in `floatConstants` instead, injected as an f64-typed named constant whose HIR Ref folds to a +inf float literal. INFINITY is +inf on ALL targets (IEEE-754 f64), so no per-target variant; math.json gates no formats (available everywhere via the all-format `library` map). c87 (D-FFI-MATH-LIBM-DT-NEEDED): the elf library is libm.so.6 — glibc ships every symbol below in libm.so.6, NOT libc.so.6 (the pre-c87 libc.so.6 entry made ld.so stop at `undefined symbol: sqrt` when loading the c86 sqlite3 binary); the ELF walker emits one DT_NEEDED per DISTINCT referenced import library, so a math.h user links libm.so.6 ALONGSIDE libc.so.6 (the CRT exit + stdio surface). ldexp moves too: libc.so.6 also exports it, but libm is a math symbol's honest home and libm.so.6 exports it as well (nm -D libm.so.6: ldexp@@GLIBC_2.2.5, single version, glibc 2.39). pe keeps msvcrt.dll and macho keeps libSystem — single-C-runtime platforms with no separate math library. VERSIONING (D-LK-ELF-SYMBOL-VERSIONING mechanism CLOSED c156 — the per-symbol `version` field emits `.gnu.version_r`; these libm symbols are LEFT UNVERSIONED BY CHOICE, being value-safe): pow/log/exp are dual-versioned in glibc (GLIBC_2.2.5 compat + GLIBC_2.29 default); DSS's unversioned refs bind the 2.2.5 compat wrappers, which route to the SAME __ieee754_* cores (values bit-identical to gcc's 2.29 binding — empirically verified c87) and differ only in SVID matherr/errno edge handling on domain errors. FC17.9(g) (D-CSUBSET-TGMATH): the 17 float VARIANTS (sqrtf…ldexpf) are C99 <math.h> symbols and the <tgmath.h> `_Generic` float-arm targets, so they ship here too (tgmath.json carries duplicate rows for standalone inclusion — first-wins-safe). fabsf/ldexpf are gated availableObjectFormats:[elf,macho]: msvcrt.dll does NOT export them (loader fails 0xC0000139 — DSS imports EVERY declared shipped extern, referenced or not); on pe the tgmath fabs/ldexp macro `variants` route their float arm through the f64 function instead (D-CSUBSET-MATH-FLOAT-VARIANTS-PE). TF-corpus cycle (SQLITE_ENABLE_MATH_FUNCTIONS): +8 double math fns the sqlite .test corpus (where.test/math1.test) exercises — cosh/sinh/tanh (C89, exported by msvcrt.dll, ungated) + log2/trunc/acosh/asinh/atanh (C99, ABSENT from msvcrt → gated availableObjectFormats:[elf,macho] like fabsf/ldexpf; on pe these SQL math functions simply do not register, the correct fail-loud, since msvcrt lacks the symbol). TF-C68 (D-FFI-OS-UNIX-LFS-ISNAN-SYMBOLS): += the `isnan` function-like MACRO. <math.h> `isnan` is a MACRO on every real platform (glibc `#define isnan(x) __builtin_isnan(x)`; the weak `isnan` in libc.so.6 is a compat leftover NOT in libm.so.6, so a `symbols` row here would plant an undefined import in libm and break the load). Shipped as the portable C fallback `((x) != (x))` — true iff x is NaN by IEEE-754 (NaN is the sole value != itself) — a pure expression needing NO symbol/library, so it works on ALL formats (elf/macho/pe) with no per-target arm and no `library` binding. sqlite util.c `sqlite3IsNaN` calls it with a side-effect-free double, so the standard fallback's twice-evaluation is safe. NEED-DRIVEN: only isnan; isinf/isfinite/fpclassify stay OUT until a consumer needs them. pe UCRT migration (pe64 full-source testfixture harness): the pe `library` binding moved msvcrt.dll -> ucrtbase.dll -- the modern Universal CRT, which unlike legacy msvcrt.dll exports the full C99 math surface natively (log2/trunc/acosh/asinh/atanh verified present in the ucrtbase.dll export table). Those five C99 fns are therefore NO LONGER gated availableObjectFormats:[elf,macho]; they register on pe now that the pe binding exports them. Math fns are stateless (pure value->value, no shared CRT global state), so sourcing them from ucrtbase.dll while the rest of the program keeps its msvcrt.dll CRT binding is safe -- no cross-runtime heap/FILE* hazard as there would be for malloc/stdio. fabsf/ldexpf STAY gated [elf,macho]: ucrtbase.dll does NOT export them either (verified absent), so importing them on pe would still fail the binary LOAD 0xC0000139 under D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-EAGER-IMPORT.

floatConstants.$comment: P69 round 4 (D-FFI-DESCRIPTOR-FLOAT-CONSTANTS-INVISIBLE-TO-THE-PREPROCESSOR): C 7.12p4 -- INFINITY 'expands to a constant expression of type float representing positive or unsigned infinity'; NAN (7.12p5) 'expands to a constant expression of type float representing a quiet NaN'; HUGE_VAL (7.12p3) is a positive DOUBLE. INFINITY was typed f64 here, so `sizeof INFINITY` was 8 and `_Generic(INFINITY, float: ...)` took no float arm, and NAN was absent. MEASURED, each reference defines all three after `#include <math.h>` alone with exactly these types (probes/mathinf.c, `_Generic` over each, exit 42): gcc 13.3.0 and clang 18.1.3 over glibc 2.39 (run 20261001-043814-1a4bac88), MSVC 19.51 and mingw-w64 13.2.0 over the UCRT (run 20261001-043838-0f23e0c9), Apple clang 21 on both Mach-O arches (run 20261001-045943-1ce3d762). Every one of them is a MACRO, which the preprocessor splices from these rows (`#ifdef INFINITY` holds) as the C front end's own constant of the stated type -- the first builtin of that type whose `lowering` is the value's (`infinity`, `quiet_nan`): `(__builtin_inff())`, `(__builtin_nanf(""))`, `(__builtin_inf())`.
floatConstants.name: INFINITY
